land.text: Wallachia as drawn in its last Cliopatria shape (1857-1858): Muntenia and Oltenia

successors.note: Wallachia 'united with Moldavia to form the United Principalities' in 1859; Cuza was voted prince of Wallachia on 5 February 1859 (24 January Old Style). Cliopatria's successor row starts in 1859.

capitals.name: Curtea de Argeș (with Câmpulung)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Câmpulung, Curtea de Argeș (1330–1418)'. Basarab I's capital Curtea de Argeș 'was destroyed during Charles I's campaign' in 1330 and he moved his seat to Câmpulung (45.27 N, 25.05 E); reconstruction of Curtea de Argeș began after 1340 (Basarab I page).

minus.text: the Banate of Severin, 'in the western part of the region' of Oltenia; Severin Fort

correction.text: Basarab's Wallachia before the seizure of the Banate of Severin: the Cliopatria shape without Mehedinți (Severin Fort), c. 1310-1313

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Basarab I's reign begins 'c. 1310' (the page also allows 'between 1304 and 1324'; first documented in a charter of 26 July 1324), four years before Cliopatria's first shape. The Banate of Severin is taken out because the page has Basarab seizing it later (ledger 1325).

minus.text: the Banate of Severin, 'in the western part of the region' of Oltenia; Severin Fort

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape without the Banate of Severin for 1314-1324; the Severin gain of 1325 (ledger) completes it, so the years 1325 onward use the full shape

keyframe_review.note: 74,561 km2. Cliopatria's shape reaches 22.50 E and so already includes the Banate of Severin, which Hungary had formed in 1233 (Oltenia page); the Basarab I page says he 'seized the Banate of Severin' and 'seems to have entirely controlled' it 'between 1324 and 1330' (disloyal to the Hungarian crown in 1325). Corrected for 1314-1324 by removing Mehedinți; the ledger's 1325 gain restores it for the last year of this shape. The infobox gives 'approximately 77,000 km2' for Wallachia without a year (ratio 0.97).

74,350 km2 (-0.3% on the 1314 shape; a re-cut, not a conquest). Covers the Battle of Posada, 9-12 November 1330, which ended Hungarian suzerainty; the infobox calls Wallachia an 'Independent state 1330–1417'.
74,350 km2, identical to 1326. Basarab I died in 1351 or 1352; the pages give no border change in 1333-1362 and the shape stands.

74,069 km2 (-0.4%): a re-cut where Cliopatria's Despotate of Dobruja and Despotate of Vidin start (both neighbours from 1363 in the seed). The page dates no territorial change in these years; Amlaș, Făgăraș and Ciceu are named as lands Wallachian princes held 'for long', but with no dates, so none are drawn. The Mircea I page (opened later) has Mircea 'granted the fiefdoms of Amlaș (Omlás) and Făgăraș (Fugurash) in Transylvania' without a date and does not mention Ciceu, so the fiefs stay undrawn.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1395 shape unchanged, valid for 1395-1399 only; from 1400 to 1404 the new keyframe principality-of-wallachia_1400 adds the Danube Delta, Dobruja and Silistra

keyframe_review.note: 74,680 km2 (+0.8%) from 1395, when Cliopatria's Ottoman Empire becomes a neighbour of Wallachia. Years only: the shape is valid 1395-1399. The page says Mircea briefly extended rule 'to the Danube Delta, Dobruja and Silistra (c. 1400-1404)', which the shape does not show, so 1400-1404 is the new keyframe _1400 and the ledger carries the gain and the loss. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1395..1399 from this entry's own 'valid for 1395-1399 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: Wallachia with 'the Danube Delta, Dobruja and Silistra', where Mircea the Elder is 'briefly extending his rule (c. 1400-1404)'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1400-1404: the Cliopatria 1402 shape plus Dobruja and Silistra (about 23,000 km2, some 30 percent of the state), which the ledger gains c. 1400 and loses c. 1404. The Mircea I page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mircea_I_of_Wallachia) instead has Mircea 'gaining Dobruja in 1388' and imposing his rule on it 'again' in 1404, so c. 1400-1404 is the Wallachia page's minimum span; neither page names the earlier holder (Cliopatria's Despotate of Dobruja ends in 1394).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1402 shape unchanged, valid for 1405-1421 only (1402-1404 is drawn with Dobruja and Silistra by the new keyframe principality-of-wallachia_1400)

keyframe_review.note: 74,280 km2. Years only: the shape is valid 1405-1421, after Mircea's hold on Dobruja ends c. 1404. The page says Wallachia 'accepted a peace treaty with the Ottomans in 1417' (infobox: independent 1330-1417, Ottoman vassal 1417-1862); suzerainty does not change the drawn area. The Ottoman Empire's dossier (me-10) should carry the vassal_start. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1405..1421 from this entry's own 'valid for 1405-1421 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]
74,280 km2 held for 107 years (1422-1528). Capital Târgoviște from 1418. 1462: 'Vlad III was defeated by Mehmed the Conqueror' at the Night Attack at Târgoviște, with no change of border on the page.
74,258 km2 (-0.03%), a re-cut. The page has Radu de la Afumați ruling four times between 1522 and 1529 and confirming Süleyman as suzerain; no territory moves.

74,327 km2. The Danube fortresses (Giurgiu, Brăila, Turnu) were Ottoman rayas until 1829 (Treaty of Adrianople page: it 'transferred the rule of the rayas of Turnu, Giurgiu and Brăila' to Wallachia); how Cliopatria treats them is not readable from the shape. Michael the Brave's 1594 conquest of Danube fortresses is in the ledger.

correction.text: Wallachia as in 1602, drawn through the civil war of 1600-1601 between Michael the Brave (Oltenia) and Simion Movilă (eastern Wallachia)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1600-1601, which Cliopatria leaves empty. In 1600 'a Polish army entered eastern Wallachia and installed Simion Movilă as ruler. Only Oltenia remained loyal to Michael'; in 1601 his son Nicolae Pătrașcu 'drove Simion Movilă out of Wallachia' and Michael was killed on 9 August 1601. The state continued, so the 1602 shape is extended back over the two years and the eastern Wallachia fighting is a contest (ledger).
74,327 km2, same as 1540-1599. The page does not cover Radu Șerban or the restoration of Ottoman suzerainty after 1601; shape stands as unverified: page budget.
74,141 km2 (-0.3%): a re-cut. Cliopatria's Principality of Transylvania row lies on the northern border to 1695 (seed); no Wallachian territorial change is dated on the pages opened.
74,188 km2, a re-cut after the Transylvanian row ends in 1695 and the Habsburg Monarchy becomes the northern neighbour (seed). Unverified: page budget.

correction.text: Wallachia without Oltenia, 1718-1738 only; unchanged shape, the years are corrected: Oltenia returns in 1739

keyframe_review.note: 50,116 km2, which is 24,164 km2 below the 74,280 km2 of 1741, matching the Oltenia infobox area of 24,095 km2: 'in 1718 under the terms of the Treaty of Passarowitz' Oltenia was 'annexed by the Habsburgs as the Banat of Craiova'. Cliopatria runs this shape to 1740, but the Treaty of Belgrade of 18 September 1739 returned it ('Oltenia was returned to Wallachia in 1739', Wallachia page; the Oltenia page says 1737, under Constantine Mavrocordatos, during the war), so the shape holds 1718-1738 and the ledger gain of 1739 restores the whole.
74,280 km2: Oltenia is back, the same area as 1402-1528. Years 1739-1740 are also whole (see _1718).

correction.text: Wallachia as in 1775, drawn through the Russian occupation (1769-1774)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1772-1774, which Cliopatria leaves empty. Russian forces took Iași on 7 October and Bucharest on 17 November (1769); the Danubian Principalities page says Catherine 'returned Wallachia, Moldavia and Bessarabia to the Ottomans in 1774, with the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca'. Wallachia stays a state under occupation, so the 1775 shape is drawn through the gap and the Russian occupation is a hatched overlay (ledger 1769-1774).
74,280 km2. Wallachia and Moldavia 'returned' to the Ottomans in 1774; the treaty made them a Russian protectorate under dual authority (Danubian Principalities page).

correction.text: Wallachia as in 1792, drawn for 1791 as well

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1791, a one-year hole in Cliopatria's record between the 1775 and 1792 shapes; the 1792 shape is extended back one year. Wallachia stays a state under the Habsburg occupation of 1789-1791: the Wallachia page has 'Habsburg troops, under Prince Josias of Coburg, again entered the country ... deposing Nicholas Mavrogenes in 1789', and the Treaty of Sistova (4 August 1791) 'returned all the territory from its conquests save the small town of Orsova' (ledger occupation_start 1789, occupation_end 1791). The pages do not say when Coburg's troops left; the end year is the treaty's.
74,280 km2; unverified: page budget.
74,374 km2 (+0.1%), a re-cut where Cliopatria's Serbs row starts in 1805 (seed). The Russo-Turkish War begins after the Porte deposed Constantine Ypsilantis in 1806.

correction.text: Wallachia as in 1812, drawn through the Russian occupation of 1806-1812

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1807-1811, which Cliopatria leaves empty: 'a 40,000-strong Russian contingent advanced into Moldavia and Wallachia' and the page names 'Russian-occupied Bucharest' (the war began on 22 December 1806). Wallachia remains a state under occupation, so the 1812 shape is drawn through the gap and the occupation is a hatched overlay (ledger).

74,374 km2. The Treaty of Bucharest of 28 May 1812 ended the occupation; the page says Russia 'returned all occupied lands other than Bessarabia', which is Moldavian land (the Bessarabia row, 1812-1813, is not Wallachia).
74,280 km2 for the single year 1814 (a re-cut between two 74,374 km2 shapes); unverified: page budget.
74,374 km2; unverified: page budget.

correction.text: Wallachia as in 1834, drawn through the Russian occupation of 1828-1834

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1828-1833, which Cliopatria leaves empty. The Russo-Turkish War (1828-1829) page has the Russian commander Wittgenstein moving 'into the Danubian Principalities' in 'April and May 1828'; the Treaty of Adrianople (14 September 1829) 'allowed Russia to occupy Moldavia and Wallachia until the Ottoman Empire had paid a large indemnity'; the Regulamentul Organic page has Kiselyov's administration 'lasting until 1 April 1834'. Wallachia stays a state, so the 1834 shape is drawn through the gap with the occupation overlay.

74,374 km2. The treaty 'fixed the border between the Ottoman Empire and Wallachia on the thalweg of the Danube' and moved the rayas of Turnu, Giurgiu and Brăila to Wallachia (ledger 1829); infobox: Regulamentul Organic 1834-1835.

correction.text: Wallachia as in 1857, drawn through the occupations of 1848-1851 and 1853-1856

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1849-1856, which Cliopatria leaves empty. The Wallachian Revolution page has Ottoman troops entering Bucharest on 25 September (13 September O.S.) 1848, a Russian force joining on 27 September and the Ottoman-Russian occupation lasting 'until 1851' (the Regulamentul Organic page says April 1851); the Crimean War page has the Russians occupying the principalities in July 1853 and evacuating them in late July 1854, when Austria occupied them for the rest of the war ('a neutral Austrian administration (1854-1856)' on the Wallachia page). Wallachia stays a state under occupation, so the 1857 shape is drawn through the gap.
74,374 km2 for 1857-1858. Cliopatria's last Wallachia shape; the union with Moldavia (5 February 1859) is the next year, and Cliopatria's United Principalities row begins in 1859.

region.text: Basarab I's core around his capital Curtea de Argeș, the heartland of Wallachia proper

ledger.note: c. 1310: Basarab I begins his reign in Wallachia. The page dates the reign 'c. 1310' or 'between 1304 and 1324'; the first document naming him is a charter of 26 July 1324 that shows him 'subject to Charles I of Hungary as the voivode of Wallachia'. The Wallachia page's infobox adds a legendary 'Dismounting by Radu Negru: 1290'.

region.text: the Banate of Severin, 'in the western part of the region' of Oltenia; Severin Fort

ledger.note: 1325: Basarab I seizes the Banate of Severin. 'Basarab became disloyal to the Holy Crown of Hungary in 1325' and 'seems to have entirely controlled the Banate of Severin between 1324 and 1330'; the page also records Hungarian control restored in 1321 and Severin Fort confirmed to Basarab in exchange for loyalty, so the exact year is soft.

region.text: the Argeș heartland where the Hungarian campaign reached the capital before Posada

ledger.note: 1330: Charles I of Hungary marches into Wallachia. The royal army destroyed Basarab's capital Curtea de Argeș 'during Charles I's campaign' before it was ambushed.
1330: Wallachian independence at Posada. 'the Wallachians ambushed the royal troops in the Battle of Posada, between the 9 and 12 November 1330', which ended 'Hungarian suzerainty in Wallachia'.

region.text: the Danube Delta, Dobruja and Silistra

ledger.note: c. 1400: Mircea the Elder reaches the Danube Delta. The page says Mircea 'briefly extended rule to the Danube Delta, Dobruja and Silistra (c. 1400–1404)'; it does not name the previous holder (Cliopatria's Despotate of Dobruja ends in 1394, so the Ottomans are taken as counterpart). The Mircea I page has Dobruja 'gained in 1388' and imposed again in 1404, so the start is the Wallachia page's c. 1400 (confidence 2); the keyframe principality-of-wallachia_1400 draws it.

region.text: the Danube Delta, Dobruja and Silistra

ledger.note: c. 1404: Mircea's hold on Dobruja ends. The same sentence closes the span at 1404 ('c. 1400–1404'). The Mircea I page says 'In 1404 Mircea was thus able to impose his rule on Dobruja again', which conflicts with a loss in 1404; the Wallachia page's span is followed.
1418: the court settles at Târgoviște, a year after Wallachia 'accepted a peace treaty with the Ottomans in 1417' (infobox: Ottoman vassal 1417-1862).

region.text: the Danube citadels Giurgiu, Brăila, Hârșova and Silistra

ledger.note: 1594: Michael the Brave storms the Ottoman Danube forts. In the autumn he 'launched a campaign against the Ottomans' and took fortresses including Giurgiu, Brăila, Hârșova and Silistra.

region.text: Transylvania, held by Michael as imperial governor

ledger.note: October 1599: Michael the Brave takes Transylvania. 'On 18 October 1599 Michael won a decisive victory' at Șelimbăr over Andrew Báthory and entered Alba Iulia as imperial governor.
May 1600: Michael the Brave enters Moldavia. His forces 'reached the capital of Iași on 6 May' and he was declared Prince of Moldavia.
1600: Michael loses Transylvania. Hungarian nobles rebelled and he was defeated at Mirăslău and 'forced out of Transylvania' (the page gives no month).
1600: Michael loses Moldavia. A Polish army under Jan Zamoyski defeated his forces, 'restoring Ieremia Movilă on the throne' (the page gives no month).
1600: Polish troops split Wallachia. A Polish army 'entered eastern Wallachia and installed Simion Movilă as ruler. Only Oltenia remained loyal to Michael.'

1601: Simion Movilă is driven out. Michael returned from Prague (23 February to 5 March 1601) and his son Nicolae Pătrașcu 'drove Simion Movilă out of Wallachia'; Michael himself was killed on 9 August 1601 near Câmpia Turzii.

region.text: the Danube citadels Giurgiu, Brăila, Hârșova and Silistra

ledger.note: 1601: the Danube forts of 1594 are back with the Ottomans. The pages opened are silent on when they were lost; the year is a bridge to the shapes of 1602 on, which show nothing south of the river. The Long Turkish War page has the Ottoman counteroffensive 'capture not only Giurgiu but also Bucharest and Târgoviște' (1595, no month) and is silent on the other forts after Michael's death, so 1601 stays a bridge.
1659: the capital moves to Bucharest (infobox: Bucharest from 1659).

region.text: Oltenia, 'Lesser Wallachia', the Banat of Craiova under the Habsburgs

ledger.note: 1716: Austrian troops hold Oltenia. By 1716 the region 'was de facto under Austrian occupation' during the Austro-Turkish War of 1716-1718.

region.text: Oltenia, 'Lesser Wallachia', the Banat of Craiova under the Habsburgs

ledger.note: 1718: the occupation becomes annexation (see the loss below).

region.text: Oltenia, 'Lesser Wallachia', the Banat of Craiova under the Habsburgs

ledger.note: 1718: Oltenia goes to the Habsburgs. 'in 1718 under the terms of the Treaty of Passarowitz' Oltenia was separated from Wallachia and annexed as the Banat of Craiova (Habsburg period 1718-1739; Wallachia page: the Ottomans 'had to concede Oltenia to Charles VI').

region.text: Oltenia, 'Lesser Wallachia', the Banat of Craiova under the Habsburgs

ledger.note: 18 September 1739: Oltenia is returned. In the Treaty of Belgrade the Habsburgs ceded 'the Banat of Craiova (modern Oltenia)' to the Ottomans; the Wallachia page says Oltenia 'was returned to Wallachia in 1739'. The Oltenia page dates the return to 1737 under Constantine Mavrocordatos, the Habsburg-held land being recovered during the war; the treaty year is used.

17 November 1769: Russia occupies Bucharest. 'November 17' is the page's date for the Russian entry into Wallachia's capital after Iași fell on 7 October 1769 (the Wallachia page dates Wallachia's first Russian occupation to 1768).

1774: Russia returns Wallachia. 'Catherine the Great returned Wallachia, Moldavia and Bessarabia to the Ottomans in 1774, with the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca' (signed 21 July 1774, RT68 page); the treaty left the principalities a Russian protectorate under dual authority.

region.text: Wallachia, with Bucharest, under the Habsburg troops of Josias of Coburg

ledger.note: 1789: 'Habsburg troops, under Prince Josias of Coburg, again entered the country during the Russo-Turkish-Austrian War, deposing Nicholas Mavrogenes in 1789.' The Austro-Turkish War (1788-1791) page has 'Josias of Saxe-Coburg conquered Bucharest' without a date. The region is the principality as a whole (the page names no part), hence confidence 2.

4 August 1791: the Treaty of Sistova; 'Austria returned all the territory from its conquests save the small town of Orsova', so the occupation of Wallachia ends. The page does not name Wallachia in the terms and does not say when the Habsburg troops left (the Convention of Reichenbach of 1790 is not on the pages opened), so the end is the treaty's.

1806: Russia reoccupies Wallachia. After the Porte deposed Constantine Ypsilantis in 1806, 'a 40,000-strong Russian contingent advanced into Moldavia and Wallachia' (the war counts from 22 December 1806; the page gives no month for the advance) and holds 'Russian-occupied Bucharest'.

28 May 1812: the Treaty of Bucharest ends the occupation. The treaty 'stipulated that Russia returned all occupied lands other than Bessarabia' (the page does not name Wallachia; the Danubian Principalities page says the principalities 'returned to Ottoman suzerainty').

April-May 1828: 'In April and May 1828, the Russian commander-in-chief, Prince Peter Wittgenstein, moved into the Danubian Principalities.' The Treaty of Adrianople (14 September 1829) then 'allowed Russia to occupy Moldavia and Wallachia until the Ottoman Empire had paid a large indemnity'; the Regulamentul Organic page has the Russian presence 'inaugurated in the first days of the war'. The page gives April and May, so no single month is entered.

region.text: the rayas of Turnu (Turnu Măgurele), Giurgiu and Brăila

ledger.note: 14 September 1829: the Danube forts come to Wallachia. The Treaty of Adrianople 'fixed the border between the Ottoman Empire and Wallachia on the thalweg of the Danube' and transferred 'the rule of the rayas of Turnu, Giurgiu and Brăila' to Wallachia.

1 April 1834: the Russian occupation ends. The Regulamentul Organic page has Kiselyov's administration 'lasting until 1 April 1834' and a peasant's reaction recorded in 1836 'upon receiving news of Russian withdrawal in 1834'; it does not describe the evacuation itself, so the month is the end of the administration (confidence 2).

27 September 1848: 'a Russian force under Alexander von Lüders joined the occupation of Bucharest, taking over administration over one half of the city', after the revolution of June 1848 was put down. 'The Ottoman-Russian occupation prolonged itself until 1851.' The Regulamentul Organic page says the occupations 'began in September 1849', which conflicts with the Revolution page and is not followed.

25 September 1848 (13 September O.S.): 'Ottoman troops headed by Omar Pasha and assisted by Fuat Pasha stormed into Bucharest'. The occupation is joint with Russia's; Wallachia was an Ottoman vassal, so the renderer may treat the two as one hatch.
April 1851: the Russian occupation ends. The Regulamentul Organic page has the Russian and Ottoman occupations of Wallachia 'both lasted until April 1851'; the Wallachia page says 'until 1851'.
April 1851: the Ottoman troops leave with the Russians (Regulamentul Organic page: the occupations 'both lasted until April 1851').
July 1853: 'The Danube campaign opened when the Russians occupied the Danubian Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia in July 1853.'

Late July 1854: 'The Russians evacuated Wallachia and Moldavia in late July 1854' (on 26 July Nicholas I, answering an Austrian ultimatum, ordered the withdrawal). No month is entered because the Austrian start that follows has no month.

1854: Austria administers Wallachia. The page gives 'a neutral Austrian administration (1854–1856)'. The Crimean War page agrees: the principalities 'were then occupied by Austria for the duration of the war'.
1856: the Austrian administration ends with the Treaty of Paris (the page pairs the Treaty of Paris with the 1854-1856 administration).
5 February 1859: Wallachia unites with Moldavia. Alexandru Ioan Cuza 'was voted prince of Wallachia on 5 February (24 January Old Style)' after the Moldavian vote, forming the United Principalities.
1859: Wallachia ends in the United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia, 'of Romania from 1862'.

wars.name: Battle of Posada
wars.outcome: Wallachian victory: Charles I's royal troops were ambushed between 9 and 12 November 1330; Hungarian suzerainty ended and Wallachia became independent.
wars.note: Charles I's campaign had destroyed the capital Curtea de Argeș before the ambush.

wars.name: Mircea I's war with Bayezid I (Battle of Rovine)
wars.outcome: No border moved on the pages opened: the Battle of Rovine (17 May 1395) is 'Disputed' in its infobox, and the page says that 'the Ottoman Empire was not able to conquer Wallachia at this time'.
wars.note: The Wallachia page dates Rovine to 1394 ('including the Battle of Rovine in 1394') and the Mircea I page to 10 October 1394; the Battle of Rovine page gives 17 May 1395, which the Ottoman dossier also uses. The war is entered from 1394 to cover both.

wars.name: Vlad III's war with Mehmed II (Night Attack at Târgoviște)
wars.outcome: No border moved on the pages opened: Mehmed II crossed the Danube at Nikopol on 4 June 1462, Vlad's Night Attack of 16-17 June failed to capture him, Mehmed entered Târgoviște at the end of June and left; Vlad was replaced by his brother Radu III in July 1462 and Wallachia paid an increased tribute.
wars.note: The Wallachia page: 'In 1462, Vlad III was defeated by Mehmed the Conqueror during his offensive at the Night Attack at Târgoviște ... accepting to pay an increased tribute.'

wars.name: Michael the Brave's campaigns

zones.text: eastern Wallachia, held by Simion Movilă in 1600-1601

wars.outcome: Michael took the Danube forts (1594), beat Sinan Pasha at Călugăreni (13 August 1595), won Transylvania (Șelimbăr, 18 October 1599) and Moldavia (May 1600), lost both and Wallachia to Hungarian nobles and Poland in 1600 and was killed on 9 August 1601.

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War of 1716-1718

zones.text: Oltenia, 'Lesser Wallachia', the Banat of Craiova under the Habsburgs

wars.outcome: Habsburg victory: by the Treaty of Passarowitz the Ottomans conceded Oltenia to Charles VI, who annexed it as the Banat of Craiova.
wars.note: Named on the Wallachia page as the Austro-Turkish War of 1716-1718; the Oltenia page dates the Austrian occupation to 1716 and the annexation to 1718.

wars.name: Austro-Russian-Turkish War of 1735-1739

zones.text: Oltenia, 'Lesser Wallachia', the Banat of Craiova under the Habsburgs

wars.outcome: The Habsburgs ceded the Banat of Craiova (Oltenia) and Belgrade to the Ottomans at the Treaty of Belgrade (18 September 1739); Oltenia returned to Wallachia.
wars.note: The Oltenia page says Oltenia was returned to Wallachia in 1737 under Constantine Mavrocordatos; the Wallachia page and the Belgrade treaty give 1739.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1768-1774)
wars.outcome: Russia occupied Moldavia (Iași, 7 October 1769) and Wallachia (Bucharest, 17 November 1769); at Küçük Kaynarca (21 July 1774) it returned the principalities and became protector of Orthodox Christians in the Ottoman Empire.

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War (1788-1791)

zones.text: Wallachia, occupied by the Habsburg troops of Josias of Coburg from 1789

wars.outcome: Wallachia was occupied by the Habsburgs in 1789 and given back: by the Treaty of Sistova (4 August 1791) 'Austria returned all the territory from its conquests save the small town of Orsova', which is not in Wallachia.
wars.note: The Wallachia page names the war the 'Russo-Turkish-Austrian War' and dates the Habsburg entry and the deposition of Nicholas Mavrogenes to 1789.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1806-1812)
wars.outcome: Russian occupation of both principalities; the Treaty of Bucharest (28 May 1812) returned all occupied lands except Bessarabia, the eastern half of Moldavia.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1828-1829)

zones.text: the rayas of Turnu, Giurgiu and Brăila

wars.outcome: The Treaty of Adrianople (14 September 1829) set the Wallachian border on the Danube thalweg, gave Wallachia the rayas of Turnu, Giurgiu and Brăila and allowed Russia to occupy the principalities until an indemnity was paid.
wars.note: The page opened gives the treaty; the war's own dates are not on it.

certainty.note: Frontiers with Hungary and Transylvania along the Carpathians, with the Golden Horde and Moldavia in the east and the Danube forts are approximate; no treaty line is dated before 1718.
The Passarowitz treaty cut off Oltenia as a Habsburg province, a line agreed by treaty.
Most of the Ottoman frontier is the Danube with Ottoman rayas on the Wallachian bank; the Moldavian boundary is not dated on the pages opened.
The Treaty of Adrianople 'fixed the border between the Ottoman Empire and Wallachia on the thalweg of the Danube'.

sources.note: Russian occupations 1769 and 1806, the 1774 and 1812 returns, protectorate status; thin on 1828-1856.

sources.title: Treaty of Adrianople (1829)
sources.note: 14 September 1829: Danube thalweg border, rayas of Turnu, Giurgiu and Brăila to Wallachia, Russian occupation until the indemnity.

sources.title: Russo-Turkish War (1768–1774)
sources.note: Russian entry into Iași (7 October 1769) and Bucharest (17 November 1769); Küçük Kaynarca 21 July 1774.

sources.title: Russo-Turkish War (1806–1812)
sources.note: Russian advance into the principalities after the 1806 deposition of Ypsilantis; Treaty of Bucharest 28 May 1812.

sources.title: Treaty of Belgrade
sources.note: 18 September 1739: the Banat of Craiova (Oltenia) ceded to the Ottomans.

sources.title: Basarab I of Wallachia
sources.note: Reign c. 1310; the 1324 charter; Banate of Severin; Battle of Posada 9-12 November 1330; capitals Curtea de Argeș and Câmpulung.

sources.title: Battle of Rovine
sources.note: Date of the battle (17 May 1395), Wallachia against Bayezid I, result disputed, no territory changed hands.

sources.title: Vlad the Impaler
sources.note: The war of 1462: Mehmed II crosses the Danube at Nikopol on 4 June, Night Attack 16-17 June, Radu III replaces Vlad in July; no territory reported to change hands.

sources.title: Austro-Turkish War (1788-1791)
sources.note: Coburg conquers Bucharest; Treaty of Sistova of 4 August 1791 returns all conquests save Orsova.

sources.title: Long Turkish War
sources.note: Michael the Brave takes Danube castles in autumn 1594; the Ottoman counteroffensive captures Giurgiu, Bucharest and Targoviste (no month); silent on the forts after 1601.

sources.title: Russo-Turkish War (1828-1829)
sources.note: Wittgenstein moves into the Danubian Principalities in April and May 1828.

sources.title: Regulamentul Organic
sources.note: Russian military presence from the first days of the 1828 war; Kiselyov administration until 1 April 1834; the Russian and Ottoman occupations until April 1851.

sources.title: Wallachian Revolution of 1848
sources.note: Ottoman troops under Omar Pasha enter Bucharest on 25 September (13 September O.S.) 1848; a Russian force joins on 27 September; the occupation lasts until 1851.

sources.title: Crimean War
sources.note: Russians occupy the Danubian Principalities in July 1853, evacuate them in late July 1854; Austria then occupies them for the duration of the war.

sources.title: Mircea I of Wallachia
sources.note: Amlas and Fagaras granted (undated); Dobruja gained in 1388 and imposed again in 1404; Rovine dated 10 October 1394.

notes: Cliopatria's Wallachia is one nearly constant shape of about 74,000 km2 (Muntenia and Oltenia plus a Danube margin) for 545 years; every area change except 1718-1740 is under 1 percent and looks like a re-cut at neighbours' changes, so the small steps are marked ok without a territorial event. Suzerainty is not drawn by this dossier: Wallachia was a Hungarian vassal in 1324 (Basarab I page: 'subject to Charles I'), independent 1330-1417 and an Ottoman vassal from 1417 (infobox 'Ottoman vassal 1417–1862', 'accepted a peace treaty with the Ottomans in 1417'); the kingdom-of-hungary and ottoman-empire dossiers should carry the matching vassal_start and vassal_end events (a Russian protectorate under dual authority from 1774 is on the Danubian Principalities page). Pages that did not give a date: Amlaș, Făgăraș, Ciceu and Hațeg north of the Carpathians ('held for long'; the Wallachia page names them without years); the Ottoman rayas of Turnu, Giurgiu and Brăila before 1829; Litovoi (died 1277 or just before 1280, an earlier polity in Oltenia c. 1247, Wallachia page) and Seneslau (not on the pages). Not reached within the nine-page budget: the Ottoman wars of Mircea the Elder (c. 1386-1418) and Vlad III (1462), the Treaty of Passarowitz page, the Russo-Turkish wars of 1828-1829 and 1853-1856, the Organic Regulation, the Austrian occupation of 1854-1856 beyond the Wallachia page's single sentence; the 1828-1833 and 1849-1856 gaps and their occupation dates are therefore low-confidence bridges. Disagreements: Oltenia's return is 1737 on the Oltenia page and 1739 on the Wallachia page and the Treaty of Belgrade (18 September 1739); the first Russian occupation is 1768 on the Wallachia page and November 1769 on the Russo-Turkish War page. Name needed by the gazetteer: Turnu Măgurele (a place, 43.75 N, 24.87 E; used as a coordinate in the 1829 gain). The Michael the Brave events treat Transylvania and Moldavia as occupations because he held them as imperial governor and prince in personal union rather than annexing them; the Transylvania and Moldavia dossiers (eu-15, eu-18) should carry the reverse events. Dossier start 1310 follows Basarab I's reign 'c. 1310'; Cliopatria's first shape begins 1314 (new keyframe _1310 covers the four years); an alternative reading puts the state's birth at independence in 1330. Repairs of 2026-10-25 (review eu-18-d): keyframes _1395 and _1402 are now adjust (years 1395-1399 and 1405-1421) with a new keyframe _1400 for 1400-1404 (Dobruja and Silistra); the Habsburg occupation of 1789-1791 and the wars of Rovine (1394/95), Vlad III (1462) and 1788-1791 were added; the occupation dates of 1828-1834, 1848-1851 and 1853-1854 now rest on the Russo-Turkish War (1828-1829), Regulamentul Organic, Wallachian Revolution of 1848 and Crimean War pages (an Ottoman occupation pair 1848-1851 was added). Unresolved: the Regulamentul Organic page puts the start of the occupations in September 1849 against September 1848 on the Revolution page; the Mircea I page dates Mircea's Dobruja to 1388 and 1404 against c. 1400-1404 on the Wallachia page; the return of the Danube forts to the Ottomans (ledger 1601) is still a bridge.
